findings.title: join() can exit without stopping flusher processes
findings.body: join() spends the entire timeout on next_step.join() first, then breaks out of the process loop as soon as the deadline has passed, before process.terminate(). The previous single-process join always terminated the flusher after the wait. With a timeout (Arroyo's join_timeout, including rebalance), every flusher process can therefore be left running. Those processes are only daemonized, not reaped, and close() intentionally does not stop them, so after partition revocation they keep calling flush_segments/produce on shards that another consumer now owns. That duplicates buffered segments to Kafka and leaves zombie processes across rebalances because nothing ever process.join()s them.

findings.title: Restart overlaps flushers and leaks the old process
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive kills a hung or dead flusher and immediately calls _create_process_for_shards, which overwrites self.processes[process_index] and self.buffers[process_index] without join()ing or waiting for the old process to exit. kill() is asynchronous, and threads (the produce_to_pipe path) are not stopped at all because terminate is gated on isinstance(..., multiprocessing.Process). Until the old worker actually dies it keeps flushing the same shards as the new one, so both can produce the same segments and race on done_flush_segments. The dropped Process handle is never reaped, so each restart also leaks a zombie and that worker's Redis/Kafka clients.

findings.title: Drift wait is a no-op, so the flush assertion is racy
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op, then calls time.sleep(0.1) after setting current_drift, with a comment that this gives the flusher time to observe the new clock. That call is the patched sleep, so it returns immediately. join() sets stopped=True before it waits, so the flusher thread must have already flushed or the test fails. The added sleep does not close that race; the test only passes if the thread is scheduled in the gap between the drift write and join().
